utterances.text: One of them is this document which was handed to us today called stipulations in relation to the testimony of Witness VG81. This is one of the problems I have with the expression stipulations. Can I just state my understanding of it and see if it agrees with yours. This of course is to avoid having to tender the statement and insofar as these statements here assist the Defence, the Prosecution accepts that the matters are as stated in this document and insofar as they assist the Prosecution, the Defence accept that they are as stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this document is just the history of it. Mr. Domazet gave us a copy yesterday asking us to agree and sign it. There were a few things that I asked. I asked that the quoted portions of the statement that were relevant be put in rather than paraphrasing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Because you wanted to be able to rely upon them so that he is accepting that they are in the statement and you are accepting the other matters which are mainly omissions from the statement, you are accepting that they are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm happy about that. Should we make this as exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think properly a Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. 34, I think, is the next number, isn't it, Mr. Domazet? That will be Exhibit D34.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, 34.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I thought you had already agreed. Yes, thank you very much. And the final matter I want to raise is a matter I asked Ms. Bauer and she was going to just check. We finally had the documents that were tested, sort of looked at with some care by the witness and there were two documents. One was a big book which only had an alphabetical list of all the patients who were dealt with and then there was a smaller one which was called the patients from the war zone or some such expression. What I wanted to make sure was at the very early part of the trial, you made a formal concession that the Prosecution had had those documents examined and were unable to challenge their authenticity. Was it -- did it include those two books P136 and 137?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Bauer very properly thought that she better not go right out on a limb without checking and I just wanted to make sure what she said tentatively was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, that there was no obvious signs of forgery in those matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, those are the matters I wanted to raise with you. Now we'll go back to your time table.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I just wanted to point out to Your Honour that the fact witness I have down for day one is in fact a witness by the pseudonym of VG87, that is the Prosecution number. We have not -- I'm sorry, VG86.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Fact witness number 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Right, on day one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the other witness is fact witness number 2 is VG97. The question arose yesterday whether statements had been provided to the Defence and I can say for VG81, 86 and 97 those statements, I believe, are in the possession Defence at least nine months at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you gave me three numbers there, 81, 86 and 97.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct. Which one is 81.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Which one is 81.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: 81 is the one I will be calling on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I see, I'm sorry. Yes, but that was the one that I asked you about, did it contain a reference to the evidence -- to the matter she's about to give evidence on?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there is no statement regarding that although Mr. Domazet, in my meetings with Mr. Domazet, I've explained the entire circumstances of that event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You see, you raised in your own defence yesterday the fact that you only worked on a few line descriptions of the Defence witnesses. That's the unfortunate consequence of the way in which the Rules are drafted, that the Defence does not have to provide statements but the Prosecution does. And that's the difference, you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, my -- the question it seems to me that the rules require me to provide statements that are in my possession. It doesn't require me to take a statement of anything that the witness may testify about. Clearly, if the investigator were to forget to ask the witness a particular question, I don't think the fact that it didn't exist in a statement would be a bar to the witness testifying about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It wouldn't, but then you see there's another principle that the Defence must be forewarned of the case you are to present and there must be some forewarning. That issue is how long and if it's not in a written statement which is obviously the safest way is that they are notified precisely of the nature of the evidence to be given. The fact that there's not a signed document is not the end to it, I agree with you there. But all of the cases, particularly a recent decision of the Appeals Chamber have made it very clear that the Defence are entitled to be forewarned of the precise nature of the evidence that the Prosecution's going to lead whereas of course the Prosecution do not get the similar benefit from the Defence who only have to give an outline of the evidence in their pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I can have the -- well, the investigator who spoke to the woman is away until the end of the month. If Mr. Domazet is -- feels he would benefit him to -- for me to write down what I've already told him, I would be more than happy to do that, but that would be my recollection of having spoken to the investigator who spoke to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't want there to be any subsequent confusion or dispute as to whether or not they have been given fair warning. That's why statements are obviously the best, but if you have given him fair warning of the nature of the evidence you anticipate that she will give, then that would be sufficient. But I just don't want there to be any dispute when she's giving evidence about this sort of matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will confirm that with Mr. Domazet and if there's anything I can do to assist him in his preparation, I will do that today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I can't imagine that she is going to take very long in her evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And that if you do have a discussion with Mr. Domazet, and if there is any problem about it, you can fill him in now so that there won't be any problem when she comes to give evidence on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally there is one witness who I have not put on the schedule -- I'm sorry, Mr. Domazet seems to want to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: After Mr. Groome, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There is one additional witness although a witness that in light of the Defence case I think will be extraordinarily important, has up until this date refused to give a statement or even to talk with us. Because of the importance of this witness, I will be making a personal trip to speak with this witness and to seek to gain her cooperation, but I just want to make the Court aware that there is the potential for one additional fact witness, that, as of now, there is no statement to provide, and there is even no commitment that she will be able to or willing to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I can see now why you don't want us to be sitting on Friday. I'm not criticising you. I'm just commenting that's all. Well, provided again that there is fair warning given to the Defence of the nature of the evidence which that witness will give, if you persuade her, I think you said, to come give it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will do that today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Right. Well, thank you for that. I expect Mr. Domazet to be producing either one or both of his witnesses first thing, that is, on the 9th of January so we can finish the Defence case before you then proceed with these others. So for the arrangements you are making you should bear in mind that he has one or perhaps two witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just one additional matter just for the purposes of formality, I will be seeking to cross-examine the radiologist and the psychiatrist who have submitted expert reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, I would understand that. Yes, Mr. Domazet, now you wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Regarding the witness that Mr. Groome mentioned just now, witnesses VG86 and VG97 whom he is planning at this stage of the proceedings. I have their statements, the statements that they gave to investigators, I received these statements before the start of the trial so this is not in dispute. What is in dispute, I believe, is why they are appearing at this stage in the re-examination when they were not suggested or proposed as evidence of the Prosecution because as far as I understood, at this stage of the proceedings, the Prosecutor could rely on witnesses which are about the defence of the accused so these statements were taken previously and they could have been used during the case in chief as witnesses of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What you're saying is that they're not properly called in reply; is that what it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely, Your Honour. I believe that at this stage of the case in reply -- of the rebuttal, they actually could have testified while the witnesses, other witnesses were testifying. So I don't understand why they are being proposed for questioning during rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm just seeing whether we had copies of them in the Prosecution documents but we don't seem to have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, they were never intended as witnesses so I doubt that they would have been submitted at the start of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I was perhaps relying on the number but we can really only determine this if it's a real issue by having a look at the statements, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I can explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What's the nature of their evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness number VG86 was also present during the statement made by the person and was present during the taping of that conversation and will testify to that. I'm sorry, VG86 -- I'm sorry, my apologies, Your Honour, I'm getting the numbers mixed up. It's VG97 is the witness who was present during that conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, then her statement -- or his statement would similarly be silent upon this matter, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The other witness, VG86 was a witness who observed the accused fall off the horse. It was provided to Mr. Domazet soon after it was taken under Rule 68. It was not appropriate or not presented in the evidence in the case in chief because it was not the Prosecution that was putting forward that he fell off a horse. It becomes relevant now because the witness saw Mr. Vasiljevic fall off a horse and will say that it occurred on the 21st or 22nd of June, a couple of days before she left Visegrad, but more importantly, she will say that it happened after several days or almost a week after another event, the disappearance of a person whom we have independent evidence already in the case in terms of the case of the Red Cross missing persons list and we can independently verify when that person disappeared. So by connecting her observations about the horse after this other person disappeared, it goes directly on point to when Mr. Vasiljevic fell off the horse and that's why we are seeking to call that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, now, Mr. Domazet, that makes it clear. VG97 is in exactly the same situation as VG81 and you would be entitled to find out from Mr. Groome in the same amount of detail what the nature of her evidence, I think it was a her, is going to be and that clearly does arise because the witness whose name we're trying not to refer to at this stage denied that he was the voice on the tape. So that would be a matter properly in reply just as VG81 is. Now that you know what VG86 is going to give evidence about, do you object to that in answer to your client's evidence as to when it happened and the evidence of these witnesses? It is, indeed, associated, I think, with the statement made by the -- or alleged to have been made by the witness on this tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. As far as Witness VG97 is concerned, if the Prosecution claims that it is a witness that can speak or tell us something about the fact and that he claims that he was present during the conversation, this is something new, it's not in the statements of the witness that I have from before because it relates to something that happened afterwards and this is why I reacted in this way. If this witness is supposed to testify to the same topic as VG86, then, yes, that is relevant at this stage. As far as Witness VG86 is concerned, if the Prosecution wishes to prove that there was, that a fall from a horse occurred which had been denied so far and that it happened on a different date, then, yes, let this witness be questioned as well. I have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, then, well there you have it. But in relation to 97, Mr. Groome, I suggest that you discuss with Mr. Domazet to make it very clear that he does understand the true nature of the evidence which she is to give which is in addition to her statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, are those the only matters that we need to dispose of at this stage? There was the consent that was signed by Mr. Domazet to this psychiatric examination. We have not so far made those exhibits but I'll have it placed as a Court document, the same as we did for the earlier orders for medical examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You've seen that, have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And if I might just say one thing regarding that examination. The only days that the doctor was available was from the 11th to the 13th. I've made it clear and asked Mr. Bruff to speak with Mr. Rohde that Mr. Vasiljevic is not to be interrupted and the doctor will not seek to examine him while we are working in Court on the Tuesday. But it might be good for the Court to also state that or to convey that to the Registry so that Mr. Vasiljevic is here as long as he isn't required in court and that then doctor will be available as soon as we are finished here in court to go to Scheveningen Detention Centre and begin the examination on the evening of the 11th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you knew the history of the troubles we've had through the Registry of getting the accused persons backwards and forwards from Scheveningen Detention Unit, you would be not even game to make that submission, but perhaps they have been cured since the problem. Basically they went one at a time and we used to have to start at 9.00, half past nine, quarter to ten so they could take the one car backwards and forwards, but I gather they have bigger vans now. I will say that the Trial Chamber hopes that the Registry will be able to arrange for him to be returned to the detention unit as soon as he's finished here in court without having to wait for the usual departure of people who are taken to the detention unit. There are a number of those vans. I've seen them coming and going now and I'm sure they will be able to arrange a special visit, a special return visit for Mr. Vasiljevic so that we are able to get on with this case. And I add to this plea to the Registry that the President has, on a number of occasions, asked me how this case is going because he is very concerned about the fact that it is going to run into next year. Yes, Mr. Domazet. Have you some problem with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, not with this, I agreed to this, the Prosecution expert witness to examine the accused and this would probably be done at the detention unit, as far as I understand. However, I just wanted to state the following: Are we still agreed to have the expert witnesses on Tuesday if Mr. Groome finds out that they are available? If it's not possible, then I request to be notified because this is then the last day and I need to know this in order to be able to plan my return to Yugoslavia. So if it is not possible to hear these expert witnesses on Tuesday, I just wanted to request then to be notified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will notify the Chamber and Mr. Domazet as soon as I receive word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, then. That means we are adjourning now until Monday at 9.30 when we will have Investigator Selsky and VG81. And hopefully on the Tuesday, we will have the two voice experts. Well, thank you very much. We'll see you on Monday. We will adjourn now. 12.30

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday the 10th day of December, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
